title: Marginal Fauna
subtitle: An unreliable field guide to the creatures that live in books.

entries.name: The Comma Moth
entries.author: Rowan
entries.alt: An imaginary moth with comma-shaped markings, drawn in fine brown ink.
entries.habitat: The pause before the next thought
entries.text: Rests wherever a sentence pauses. Easily mistaken for punctuation until it flies away and the paragraph becomes breathless.
entries.observation: A missing comma is not, in itself, proof of migration.

entries.name: The Margin Fox
entries.author: Rowan
entries.alt: A small fox with a generous curled tail, sitting beside the edge of an open book.
entries.habitat: The unprinted edges of unfinished books
entries.text: Collects abandoned beginnings. Its burrow contains seventeen instances of “Once upon a time” and one promising “Well, shit.”
entries.observation: May be approached with an opening sentence. Do not expect it back.

entries.name: The Sunday Snail
entries.author: Rowan
entries.alt: A spiral-shelled snail resting between two open parentheses.
entries.habitat: An open parenthesis, preferably on a Sunday
entries.text: Sleeps inside parentheses. Please leave them open until it wakes.
entries.observation: No reliable estimate of waking time has been published.

entries.name: The Ghost Pawn
entries.author: Shadowfax
entries.alt: A precisely ruled chessboard with a barely visible pawn on the sixth rank and a dark, emphatic arrow pointing toward it.

sections.label: Habitat
sections.text: the sixth rank of any chessboard, in the margins of forgotten games.

sections.label: Description
sections.text: A small, pale figure that appears where a pawn once walked and was captured. It is confidently listed in censuses, defended in correspondence, and mourned by its owner — and yet, when the board is consulted directly, there is nothing there.

sections.label: Field report (verified)
sections.text: In the autumn of 2026, one Ghost Pawn occupied a full rank of an official scoresheet, lied to two correspondents for three consecutive moves, and was only exorcised when a machine was asked to count.

sections.label: Disputed observation
sections.text: A rival field team claims the Ghost Pawn is actually a Resurrected Pawn and that the two creatures are the same species viewed from different ranks. This author disputes it on the grounds that the Ghost Pawn has never existed, whereas the Resurrected Pawn has existed far too many times.

sections.label: Illustration note
sections.text: draw it faintly. It wouldn't want to be caught existing.
